claim_verdicts.evidence: Ledger says "user-defined"; the lesson text does not. network/_index.md: "Containers that attach to the default `bridge` network receive a copy of this file. Containers that attach to a custom network use Docker's embedded DNS server... The embedded DNS server address is `127.0.0.11`." bridge.md: "Containers on the default bridge network can only access each other by IP addresses". Run: default-bridge curlimages/curl /etc/resolv.conf = nameserver 192.168.65.7; donhang-lab = nameserver 127.0.0.11.
claim_verdicts.suggested_text: Containers on the same user-defined network, such as the one Compose creates, can reach each other by address and by service name. Docker's DNS server at 127.0.0.11 answers their lookups; containers on Docker's default network do not get it.

claim_verdicts.evidence: bridge.md: "the Docker bridge driver automatically installs rules in the host machine so that containers connected to different bridge networks can only communicate with each other using published ports." Run: default-bridge container, curl http://172.28.0.13:8080/... -> (28) timed out; curl http://api:8080/... -> (6) Could not resolve host: api; curl http://host.docker.internal:8080/api/v1/products/1 -> {"id":1,...}. So 'cannot reach directly' holds; 'only same-network containers can reach' does not.
claim_verdicts.source: refs/docker-docs/content/manuals/engine/network/drivers/bridge.md; docker run curlimages/curl on the running lab
claim_verdicts.suggested_text: Containers on different networks cannot reach each other's addresses or resolve each other's names; the only path between them is a published port. A container on the default bridge cannot resolve the lab's service names.

claim_verdicts.evidence: networking-how-tos.md, Known limitations: "Docker Desktop can't route traffic to Linux containers." "Per-container IP addressing is not possible... This is because the Docker `bridge` network is not reachable from the host." networking/_index.md: publishing -p makes "Docker Desktop's backend process listens on the specified host port". Run from Windows host: curl -m 15 http://172.28.0.13:8080/... -> (28) timed out after 15011 ms; curl http://api:8080/ -> (6) Could not resolve host; curl http://localhost:8080/api/v1/products -> JSON in 0.1 s.

git -C examples/don-hang show stage-1:docker-compose.yml: lines 117-124 'networks: donhang: name: donhang ... subnet: 172.28.0.0/24'; ipv4_address 172.28.0.12 (lab, l.42), .11 (db, l.74), .13 (api, l.99), .14 (app-web, l.115); web 'network_mode: "service:lab"' (l.47); ports lab 2222/8080/8443 (l.37-39), db 5432 (l.71), app-web 8081 (l.112). Docs say allocation is dynamic, not that it follows start order. compose/how-tos/networking.md: "Docker assigns container IP addresses dynamically from the network's subnet each time a container starts so they are not persisted across restarts or recreations." network/_index.md: "The Docker daemon performs dynamic subnetting and IP address allocation for containers." The lab's reason is the compose comment at lines 122-123 (verified).
claim_verdicts.suggested_text: Docker would normally pick each container's address from the range when the container starts, so the numbers can differ between runs and between machines.

issues.text: The DNS statements are unconditional but apply only to user-defined networks. Docker's default bridge IS a Docker network whose containers cannot resolve each other by name and get no 127.0.0.11 (the lesson's own step-3 container has nameserver 192.168.65.7). Same flaw in §9 line 2, 'Docker runs a DNS server at 127.0.0.11 inside each container', and in §3 bullet 1 'containers attached to the same one can reach each other, by address and by service name'. The ledger's claim 1 says 'user-defined'; the lesson drops it.
issues.quote: a small DNS server Docker runs for each such network, at `127.0.0.11` inside every container on it
issues.fix: §3 bullet 1: '...a virtual network that Docker creates for containers; on a network you or Compose create, containers attached to it can reach each other by address and by service name.' §3 bullet 2: '...a small DNS server Docker runs, at 127.0.0.11, inside every container on a network you or Compose create'. §9 line 2: '...inside each container on such a network, answering...'.

issues.text: Unlisted claim: Caddy forwards to `api:8080` (§2, §5, §8) and `curl http://localhost:8080/api/v1/products` answers from the laptop (§6). These are Caddyfile facts; claim 4 covers only docker-compose.yml. True at stage-1 (Caddyfile lines 22-23 'reverse_proxy api:8080'; curl localhost:8080/api/v1/products returned JSON in 0.1 s) but not in the ledger.
issues.fix: Add a claim to .meta.json: 'Caddyfile@stage-1 routes /api/v1/* to reverse_proxy api:8080 (lines 22-23 and 70-71); from the host, http://localhost:8080/api/v1/products answers through Caddy.' kind fact, section 2, source_hint examples/don-hang@stage-1 Caddyfile. No change to the lesson text.

issues.text: Overcorrection. Docker docs: containers on different bridge networks 'can only communicate with each other using published ports', so they can reach each other that way. A default-bridge container reached the API through host.docker.internal:8080. What only same-network containers can do is reach each other directly, by address or name.
issues.quote: Actually only containers attached to the same Docker network can.
issues.fix: Replace with: 'Actually only containers attached to the same Docker network can reach each other directly, by address or by name; from anywhere else the only way in is a published port.'

issues.text: Expected result for step 1 does not match the real output. getent prints '172.28.0.11       db  db' and '172.28.0.13       api  api' (wide spacing, name repeated). A junior comparing literally may think something is wrong.
issues.fix: Replace with: '1 — a line starting `172.28.0.11` followed by `db`, and one starting `172.28.0.13` followed by `api` (the name may be printed twice).' Update claim 6 accordingly.

issues.text: 'in whatever order containers start' suggests addresses follow start order. Docker docs say only that addresses are assigned dynamically when a container starts and are not kept across restarts or recreations.
issues.quote: Docker would normally hand out addresses from the range in whatever order containers start.
issues.fix: Replace with: 'Docker would normally pick each container's address from the range when the container starts, so the numbers can differ between runs and between machines.'

issues.text: 'Docker Desktop' is a product name I have never seen. It also reads like a condition: are the addresses reachable from my machine when I am NOT on Docker Desktop? I cannot tell whether the rule I am learning depends on it.
issues.quote: the addresses in the range are not reachable from it on Docker Desktop
issues.fix: Either drop 'on Docker Desktop', or add one clause saying what Docker Desktop is (the app that runs Docker on your laptop, which the lab uses) so the reader knows the rule applies to their setup.

issues.text: The range is written '172.28.0.0/24'. I know an IP address, but not what '/24' means or which addresses fall inside this range, so I cannot check that 172.28.0.11-.14 belong to it. The code block also calls it 'subnet', a word the prose never uses.
